skill.name: swiftui-expert-skill
skill.description: Build, review, and modernize SwiftUI code with guidance for state management, view composition, performance, navigation, text formatting, image handling, and iOS 26 Liquid Glass patterns.
skill.summary: SwiftUI guidance for modern APIs, state management, performance, navigation, and Liquid Glass adoption.
skill.author: avdlee

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged markdown backticks, SwiftUI UI terms, and one example URL. Review found these are documentation examples and references, with no executable scripts, shell commands, network calls, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

static_findings.snippet: // Unsafe - force unwrap can crash if imageData is invalid
// Avoid - magic numbers that don't adapt
Liquid Glass is Apple's new design language introduced in iOS 26. It provides translucent, dynamic s
All Liquid Glass APIs require iOS 26 or later. Always provide fallbacks:
// Interactive glass - responds to user interaction
// Avoid (unless you need a specific weight)
// Avoid - type erasure has performance cost
**Avoid using UIKit colors in SwiftUI code.**
**Avoid passing large "config" or "context" objects.** Pass only the specific values each view needs
**Keep view body simple and pure.** Avoid side effects, dispatching, or complex logic.
- [ ] Pass only needed values to views (avoid large config objects)
// Avoid - boolean flag requires separate state
// Avoid - parent manages sheet actions via closures
- [ ] Avoid passing dismiss/save callbacks to sheets
// Avoid - breaks animations and change tracking
- Check property wrapper usage against the selection guide (see `references/state-management.md`)
- Verify view composition follows extraction rules (see `references/view-structure.md`)
- Verify list patterns use stable identity (see `references/list-patterns.md`)
- Inspect Liquid Glass usage for correctness and consistency (see `references/liquid-glass.md`)
- Audit state management for correct wrapper selection (prefer `@Observable` over `ObservableObject`
- Replace deprecated APIs with modern equivalents (see `references/modern-apis.md`)
- Extract complex views into separate subviews (see `references/view-structure.md`)
- Refactor hot paths to minimize redundant state updates (see `references/performance-patterns.md`)
- Suggest image downsampling when `UIImage(data:)` is used (as optional optimization, see `reference
- Design data flow first: identify owned vs injected state (see `references/state-management.md`)
- Use modern APIs (no deprecated modifiers or patterns, see `references/modern-apis.md`)
- Use `@Observable` for shared state (with `@MainActor` if not using default actor isolation)
- Structure views for optimal diffing (extract subviews early, keep views small, see `references/vie
- Separate business logic into testable models (see `references/layout-best-practices.md`)
- Apply glass effects after layout/appearance modifiers (see `references/liquid-glass.md`)
- Gate iOS 26+ features with `#available` and provide fallbacks
- **Mark `@Observable` classes with `@MainActor`** unless using default actor isolation
- **Never declare passed values as `@State` or `@StateObject`** (they only accept initial values)
- `@Binding` only when child needs to **modify** parent state
- Use `let` for read-only values; `var` + `.onChange()` for reactive reads
- Nested `ObservableObject` doesn't work (pass nested objects directly); `@Observable` handles nesti
- Use `.sheet(item:)` instead of `.sheet(isPresented:)` for model-based content
- Sheets should own their actions and call `dismiss()` internally
- Use `ScrollViewReader` for programmatic scrolling with stable IDs
- Use modern Text formatting (`.format` parameters, not `String(format:)`)
- Use `.task` modifier for automatic cancellation of async work
- Keep view `body` simple and pure (no side effects or complex logic)
- Use `@ViewBuilder` functions only for small, simple sections
- Prefer `@ViewBuilder let content: Content` over closure-based content properties
- Avoid redundant state updates in `onReceive`, `onChange`, scroll handlers
- Use stable identity for `ForEach` (never `.indices` for dynamic content)
- Ensure constant number of views per `ForEach` element
- Avoid inline filtering in `ForEach` (prefilter and cache)
- Suggest image downsampling when `UIImage(data:)` is encountered (as optional optimization)
- Use `Self._printChanges()` to debug unexpected view updates
- Use native `glassEffect`, `GlassEffectContainer`, and glass button styles
- Apply `.glassEffect()` after layout and visual modifiers
| `@State` | Internal view state (must be `private`), or owned `@Observable` class |
| `onChange(of:) { value in }` | `onChange(of:) { old, new in }` or `onChange(of:) { }` |
- [ ] Using `@Observable` instead of `ObservableObject` for new code
- [ ] Passed values NOT declared as `@State` or `@StateObject`
- [ ] `@Binding` only where child modifies parent state
- [ ] Nested `ObservableObject` avoided (or passed directly to child views)
- [ ] Using `ScrollViewReader` with stable IDs for programmatic scrolling
- [ ] Container views use `@ViewBuilder let content: Content`
- [ ] View `body` kept simple and pure (no side effects)
- `references/view-structure.md` - View composition, extraction, and container patterns
- `references/list-patterns.md` - ForEach identity, stability, and list best practices
- `references/layout-best-practices.md` - Layout patterns, context-agnostic views, and testability
- `references/modern-apis.md` - Modern API usage and deprecated replacements
- `references/text-formatting.md` - Modern text formatting and string operations
- We emphasize thread safety with `@MainActor` and `@Observable`
description: Write, review, or improve SwiftUI code following best practices for state management, v

- Pass only needed values to views (avoid large "config" or "context" objects)

content.value_statement: SwiftUI projects can accumulate deprecated APIs, fragile state, and slow view updates. This skill gives focused guidance for modern, maintainable SwiftUI code.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SwiftUI state management and property wrapper choices.
Suggests modern replacements for deprecated SwiftUI APIs.
Guides view extraction, composition, and layout decisions.
Identifies performance risks in lists, body work, and state updates.
Provides patterns for sheets, navigation, scrolling, text formatting, and image optimization.
Explains iOS 26 Liquid Glass usage with availability fallbacks.
limitations: Does not run or compile Swift projects by itself.
Does not replace Apple documentation for final platform checks.
Focuses on SwiftUI guidance, not UIKit-heavy architecture decisions.
Liquid Glass guidance applies only when the target platform supports it.

use_cases.title: Review a SwiftUI Feature
use_cases.description: Find state, navigation, layout, and performance issues before merging a feature.

use_cases.title: Modernize Legacy Views
use_cases.description: Replace older SwiftUI APIs with current patterns while preserving behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan a New App Screen
use_cases.description: Design data flow, view structure, and platform fallbacks before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Review My View
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one SwiftUI file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI view for state management, deprecated APIs, accessibility, and simple performance issues. Explain the highest priority fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for Modern SwiftUI
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this SwiftUI screen to use modern APIs. Preserve behavior, explain each change, and call out any iOS version requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Improve List Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnose slow scrolling or frequent updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this SwiftUI list for identity, filtering, state updates, and body computation problems. Recommend focused changes that reduce redraw work.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complex Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for navigation, sheets, and async work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SwiftUI implementation plan for this flow. Include state ownership, navigation types, sheet presentation, async task handling, and fallback strategy.

output_examples.input: A SwiftUI profile screen that uses older navigation, color styling, and several local state values.
output: A prioritized review of outdated API usage.
State ownership recommendations for local and shared data.
A short migration plan for navigation and styling.

output_examples.input: A scrolling feed with inline filtering, image decoding, and unstable item identity.
output: A performance diagnosis focused on identity and body work.
Recommendations to prefilter data and stabilize identifiers.
Optional image downsampling guidance for large images.

output_examples.input: A request to add iOS 26 Liquid Glass to a toolbar.
output: A platform-gated approach using native glass effects.
Fallback guidance for earlier iOS versions.
Notes on where interactive glass is appropriate.

best_practices: Share the target iOS version and backward compatibility constraints.
Provide complete SwiftUI view context, including models and navigation state.
Ask for prioritized findings when reviewing large or complex screens.
anti_patterns: Do not request Liquid Glass unless the feature explicitly needs it.
Do not treat suggestions as compiled proof without running Xcode checks.
Do not provide isolated snippets when the issue depends on shared state.

faq.question: Can this skill write new SwiftUI code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help plan and draft SwiftUI views using modern APIs and platform-aware patterns.

faq.question: Does it support older iOS versions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes legacy guidance and recommends availability checks when newer APIs are used.

faq.question: Can it review performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on view identity, state updates, body work, lists, and image handling.

faq.question: Does it enforce a specific architecture?
faq.answer: No. It encourages testable business logic without requiring a named architecture.

faq.question: Can it compile or run my app?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and code suggestions, but build verification must happen in your development environment.

faq.question: When should I use the Liquid Glass guidance?
faq.answer: Use it only for iOS 26 or later designs, and include fallbacks for earlier supported versions.
